item.title: King’s parting words in Germany touch a heart, inspire pledge to...
item.description: A Tongan woman in Germany has made an emotional pledge to King Tupou VI after His Majesty’s parting words during his recent royal visit left a lasting impression on her heart. The King and Queen Nanasipauʻu visited Germany to commemorate the 150th anniversary of the Treaty of Friendship between Germany and Tonga, first signed on 1 November 1876.
item.content:encoded:
A Tongan woman in Germany has made an emotional pledge to King Tupou VI after His Majesty’s parting words during his recent royal visit left a lasting impression on her heart.

The King and Queen Nanasipauʻu visited Germany to commemorate the 150th anniversary of the Treaty of Friendship between Germany and Tonga, first signed on 1 November 1876.

The visit also provided an opportunity for Their Majesties to meet members of the Tongan diaspora, including those who travelled from other European countries, such as Spain, to join the gathering in Berlin.

It was during this gathering that the King delivered a speech appealing to the Tongan community to preserve its language, culture and heritage — a message that resonated deeply with one woman.

“Teach your children and grandchildren the Tongan language. Let the Tongan language never disappear, let us never forget our Tongan culture, and let our Tongan heritage never be lost,” His Majesty reportedly said.

For Mele Wiebe, those words became a personal call to action.

“His Majesty’s final words before his departure touched me deeply and left a lasting impression on my heart,” she wrote on Facebook.

“Your Majesty, we will do our very best to carry on the message you have entrusted to us. We will teach our children and grandchildren so they know who they are, where they come from, and always take pride in being Tongan.”

Wiebe described their roots as a treasure, their heritage as an inheritance, and its preservation as a responsibility owed to future generations.

“May your words become a legacy passed down from generation to generation. May the Tongan language live on. May our culture never fade. And may the Tongan spirit remain strong in the hearts of our children and grandchildren, forever.”

Wiebe’s tribute adds another dimension to the personal stories emerging from the royal visit, highlighting the enduring connection between Tongans living in Germany and their ancestral homeland.

Kaniva News previously reported how Patrick Muller’s proud display of the Tongan flag from the roadside as the royal motorcade passed culminated in a memorable encounter in which he shook hands with King Tupou VI.

Another report featured Elina Moana Nive Malia, originally from Longoteme, who moved to Germany in 1978. After nearly half a century overseas, the royal gathering in Berlin brought her family together with fellow Tongans in a celebration that evoked the feeling of being back home in the kingdom.
